Much has changed over the first game, which I enjoyed a lot. And I am happy to say that it changed for the better. Game got improved in many areas, multiple systems now make more sense and depend on many new things. Besides, we got airborn creatures as well as underwater ones, which is epic.
Also, it is easier to manage the dinosaurs and keep them happy and not running away all the time.

The biggest problems by far is with controls. I can't get into it, UI is sometime unintuitive, almost like actively fighting against you. For example, when I click "R", it selects Response team building, but then I have to click which team I want to use and if I want to start driving it directly or give them orders. In first game, I pressed "R", it chose ranger team closest to my area and I could start clicking what I wanted and start giving orders.
Second problem I have is the forest demand of all dinosaurs. Most of the time, they require 70+% of forest area to be happy, which is ridiculous, because you have this massive area covered with forests through which you cant see anything. Gets tiresome very quickly. Apart from that, I am very happy with the game so far.

In my opinion, this is frontier's best work. I have played a couple other games by them, and this one is by far my favorite. The way the dinos move is amazingly realistic, and there are some especially well done animations, my favorites including the Ankylosaurus/ankylodocus interaction, the dunkleosteus and megalodon shark feeding, and the therizinosaurus kill animation against large and medium carnivores. I understand that all of these animation require at least one DLC, and I think that goes to show that the DLCs also have a lot of work put into them. This is also one of the only official JW games out there. However, I don't think that is worth sixty dollars. But if its on sale, I think you should buy it.

Note: The fact that this is my favorite movie franchise and how much I like park building games didn't make this bias at all. (totaly)

Loved the first one and this sequel is in every way an improvement. Improved graphics are just the start. No more need to send your rangers willy-nilly to fill feeders. They're automated. And sure, you start with power generators that require you to refill them every so often, but soon enough you can upgrade to powerplants. More custom features for shops & restaurants. And one feature alone makes this game better than the original: a pause button. There's still the potential for sabotage and storms to disrupt what you're doing, and you need to manage your money smartly, but when things are humming it is just like you'd imagine. Plenty of time to wander the park and enjoy the dinos, take some pictures. In short, perfection. The only thing missing? A breeding and trading feature akin to Planet Zoo.

Amazing game! As a person who fell in love with Jurassic Park as a teenager and played all kind of strategy games, this game is INCREDIBLE. I can't stop playing it since I got it. It's quite impressive when I remember the quality of old games, where poligons and pixels were huge and I find out that here, not only it looks incredible, but the fact that I can zoom in on the dinosaurs and see them really close in high detail, their animations and movements are quite well done, and on top of that, you can select vehicles like cars and helicopters and control them in first person and you can feel the size of everything you've built, drops my jaw. 

And on top of that, it has the music scores from John Williams and voice overs from the film actors, including Jeff Goldblum! What else could I ask for? This game is a must, I love it!!!

How do I say this... This game purely still exists due to the modding community providing us with basic tools and assets which should be in the game. Mods including no barriers due to the stupid limitations, raptor, rex, indominus paddock models and more. Biggest highlight being the terrain brushes and tools. I've taken a break for 8 months to realise no mods have been updated but my game is deciding to throw a tantrum. I've been getting weird bugs like my scientist vanishing etc, with no way of finding out which mod is causing the issue. This isn't the usual turn on crash and start removing mods. These bugs are appearing 4 hours down my challenge mode also resulting in another bug stopping me from saving.

Yes, maybe its my fault for modding. But you don't understand the need for them until you see how much they offer vs this empty game. I really hope they setup a mod support in the next one, as I am tired of these headaches each time I want to play. Offering a modding community hub would be the right step forward with some tools to highlight which mods are playing up.

Good graphics, decent gameplay (kind of tycoonish), and some alright voice acting. The dinosaurs look really good with their own little interactions with each other and their own needs depending on the species, which can lead to some diverse scenery and enclosures. My only issue is the park size. You're given an area that seems like a good size but the boundaries start at odd point around the maps. Its especially apparent when you're in a mountainous area. This wouldn't be too big of a problem if the dinosaurs didn't require so much space. When you try to expand, the boundaries will be at weird angles and will sometimes start and end at places where there clearly should (and is) more space. This might not be as big of an issue in other maps, but if you're just starting out you're probably not going to have much space for the park you want.

If you're into creating your own dino-filled paradise, Jurassic World Evolution 2 is definitely worth a try. The game offers stunning graphics that make the dinosaurs and the park come alive, with a relaxing atmosphere that's perfect for those who enjoy a more laid-back experience. The gameplay is engaging, allowing you to immerse yourself in decorating and managing your park, from building enclosures to ensuring your guests are having a good time.

However, there are a few bugs that can dampen the experience. Vehicles sometimes struggle to find a path into enclosures, despite having multiple gates available, which can be frustrating when you're trying to manage your park smoothly. Dinosaurs, especially smaller ones, occasionally glitch out of their fences and end up outside the park, which not only looks odd but can also cause havoc. The aviary creatures sometimes get stuck in place, leading them to starve or die, which is really disappointing when you're trying to maintain a healthy and thriving park.

On top of that, guests sometimes gather in one spot and don't move, creating unrealistic crowds that break the immersion. These issues can be a bit annoying, but they don't overshadow the overall enjoyment of the game. Despite the bugs, I still love Jurassic World Evolution 2 and would recommend it to anyone who enjoys park management games, especially with a dino twist. Just be prepared to encounter some quirks along the way!

Hire a genetic engineering specialist to research a wider walking path.

Grind through endless celebrity cameo missions to piecemeal your way through the same content over and over again.

Manually refuel buildings, because you are part park manager and part minimum wage maintenance worker.

Suffers from a lack of clear vision in the gameplay loop, preposterous amounts of micromanagement, and the dead weight of the franchise.

The game would be fantastic, and I would recommend it, if they cut a bunch of unnecessary content and had all sandbox content unlocked from the start.

That being said if you have hours to spend listening to voice actors and being taught the same basic gameplay loop over and over again, and love the idea of being cornered in a dark alley and mercilessly bludgeoned into a fine dead horse pulp with tedious cookie clicker mechanics, there's a great dinosaur park building game floating around in there... if you can find the time to enjoy it before your scientists demand a $75,000 nap.

This new iteration has improved on a lot of things, interaction among the dinosaurs, being first imo. But the amount of bugs and simple carelessness with game design is appalling. Multiple save-ending bugs exist, forcing you to lose everything restarting. And its like they didn't even try and play using the current camera design. Clicking or choosing almost anything auto-forces your camera to certain angles, usually zoomed all the way out. Spent a minute getting close and looking at this cool thing? Don't dare try and click first-person view otherwise you are immediately zoomed all the way out to choose where to put yourself.

Overall, most aspects are improved. But the ones that got worse make it, at times, literally unplayable. Don't spend more than $20, and even thats probably high.

Game has a well known hard crash issue, that forces a full PC reset; The kind of crash that makes you feel like you just bricked your PC, basically.
There are threads going as far back as 2021 talking of this exact issue, with no fix ever mentioned; And further instabilities brought about with the latest video driver updates and game being incompatible.

I loved what I played of it, but I cannot give this a recommendation until these issues are fixed... I will also be refunding the game, because I cannot, in good contience, put my PC at risk for it.

Will add that, if this crashing/freezing issue gets fixed or people in discussion forums point me towards how to avoid it/fix it, I will rebuy the game and change my review into a positivie one.
I legitimately loved what I played that much.

tldr.text: Very Positive (90%): players love the graphics and art, and many think the game is worth it on sale.
The price, bugs and crashes draw the most complaints.

details.text: Newer players are far less positive than long-time players: 56% of them are positive, against 95% of those with the most hours.
One review flags the Denuvo anti-tamper inclusion as a reason for a thumbs down, which matters to buyers who object to that protection.
